title: Supersession with access-based recency for task records
context: Task records accumulate over time. Older but still-valid records that have been re-verified were cluttering delivery, while truly stale records got equal weight to frequently-used ones. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_03a0b94b2e (The agent hook must never block an edit on failure: any error exits 0 and never denies; after the event is recognized it emits at most one 'grounding unavailable' context line, unrecognized input emits nothing); con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_91e6074b66 (Capability pages for functionality shipped in the current release must state that it ships today and must not retain the stale banner 'In development for the next release.'); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Introduce supersession: a newer task that re-checks the same file/rule and passes marks older tasks as superseded (never delivered); recency now counts from the later of finish time and last delivery, keeping frequently-delivered tasks warm via access-based decay.
consequences: Older verified work is hidden by newer verification, reducing delivery clutter without deleting records
Frequently-delivered task lines stay warm and rank higher even after weeks, mirroring how useful knowledge persists in practice
Ranking now depends on delivery receipts (new database queries), adding a dependency on served ledger
Append-only invariant preserved: no records deleted, only marked unreachable via supersedes field
alternatives_rejected: Delete old records: breaks append-only guarantee and auditability
Retain all records with time-only decay: old but active work gets buried as it ages
Only time-based recency without delivery tracking: doesn't distinguish frequently-used from forgotten records
